angle: It scores both classes fully in log space on continuous snack features with per-class Gaussians, letting one dominant feature visibly overturn the verdict the other features suggest.
angle_detail: Start with the per-class Gaussian setup at [01:14] to [02:22] to see how each snack amount becomes a distribution per class. Then follow the loves-class scoring at [03:33] to [05:19], where the log transform against underflow is introduced, against the not-loves scoring at [05:19] to [07:12]. It assumes multinomial Naive Bayes and the likelihood-versus-probability distinction from [00:32], so review those first; priors here are just 0.5 each.
